prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: FINAL cohesive public-bathroom concept review image for an existing 2D old Chinese factory/prison exploration game.
Input images: Image 1 is a current bathroom scene REFERENCE for game camera, existing wooden bench, lockers, pipes and the south entrance. Image 2 is the approved clinic STYLE REFERENCE for painterly detail, subdued colors, game architecture and the exact orange-uniform chibi player's identity and scale. Neither is a literal edit target. Design a NEW bathroom concept using the approved brief below.
Composition: ONE wide landscape image with TWO equally detailed side-by-side full-building views at IDENTICAL camera and scale. LEFT: the bathroom with the roof hidden, revealing the complete furnished interior. RIGHT: the EXACT SAME bathroom, footprint, south wall and doorway, with its new roof closed. Clean subdued grey-green factory pavement backdrop, modest margins, full building visible in both panels, no cropped corners. Simple small Chinese headings above the panels, exactly "室内方案" and "屋顶方案"; no diagram callouts or technical UI. Treat this as a polished game-scene mockup, not a photoreal architectural render.
Projection/style: orthographic elevated TOP-DOWN 2D game view like the reference clinic, rectangular floor, walls and equipment aligned perfectly to horizontal/vertical screen axes; no isometric diamond, vanishing point or 3D dollhouse camera. Shallow painted wall elevation is visible on the north/south faces. Crisp hand-painted edges and subtle drawn outlines; detailed but calm surfaces, soft diffuse daylight. Same slightly worn old factory universe as the approved clinic.
Building scale: compact NARROW RECTANGULAR bathroom, approximate usable interior ratio440:540 world units. Standard player height84 world units, so the orange-uniform man is about one sixth of the usable floor's north-south length, matching the clinic reference. Do not enlarge the character or make oversized furniture. All walls are thin ivory coping with blue-grey narrow trim and clean continuous45-degree mitred corners, no thick stone rounded prison caps, no tall metal corner posts.
Bathroom wall identity: warm off-white plaster above cool grey-blue or pale aqua glazed ceramic tile wainscot covering the lower two thirds of the wall faces. Fine straight grout, damp wear and lime deposits localized near pipes and floor edges. A small high frosted window at the north wall, simple warm-white utility wall lamp, and one modest cream enamel sign reading exactly "公共浴室", no medical crosses.
LEFT interior layout:
- EXACTLY SIX individual shower bays arranged in TWO COLUMNS of THREE bays: three down the WEST/left wall and three down the EAST/right wall, occupying the upper/north60% of the room. Each column runs vertically on screen. All shower positions open toward a straight central north-south aisle. Do not put six showerheads in one horizontal row.
- Each bay has one dark aged steel shower pipe, one recognizable metal showerhead projecting inward from its service wall, one small valve, a shallow flush square pale ceramic standing area and a small floor drain. Shower equipment follows the respective wall orientation; pipes are not isolated bath tubs or giant machines. Low tiled partition fins divide adjoining bays while leaving the central aisle fully open. All six standing spaces are visibly accessible from the aisle. No high doors, cubicle roofs, curtains or full-height dividers.
- Clear continuous central passage around100–120 world units wide, from the SOUTH entrance to the north end of the shower area. No cabinet, bench or partition obstructs it.
- Lower/south40% is a compact dry changing zone. One small row of four dark grey-blue numbered lockers sits against the southwest wall, FRONT faces readable with small vents and restrained wear. A modest old wooden bench holding folded towels and one pair of dark slippers sits near the southeast side, clear of the centre passage. One small woven linen basket rests beside the bench near the edge.
- Distinguish wet and dry floor using closely related pale grey-blue antislip ceramic tiles, slightly lighter dry floor near the entrance, small neat drainage channels near shower bases. Tiny localized damp sheen only, no large dirty puddles or giant empty patch of floor.
- ONE familiar fully clothed spiky-black-haired orange prison-uniform chibi player stands in the centre aisle near the changing zone, visible full-body, no selected-circle, head and body naturally in same layer. No other people and no bathing or unclothed people.
- SOUTH entrance: a wide open centre doorway, about180 world units wide, slim grey-blue jambs integrated into the low front tiled facade, clear passage matching the existing bath entrance. NO opened door leaves, grille, threshold obstacle or crossbeam blocking the walking route.
RIGHT closed-roof view:
- Same exact compact building and south doorway, same tiled front facade, with the interior and player completely hidden by a dedicated pale COOL GREY-BLUE waterproof flat roof.
- Quiet broad roof surface, three understated horizontal expansion joints, restrained weathering only along the edges. Not the beige gritty concrete of neighbouring prison roofs, not corrugated warehouse roofing, not a ceramic floor-tile grid.
- TWO small low blue-grey exhaust vents on discreet square metal bases in the upper roof area, one above each shower bank; one tiny neat drainage outlet near a rear edge. Sparse low fittings, readable at game size. Blue-grey continuous perimeter flashing matches the ivory thin wall coping and clean four corners. No skylight required, no giant tanks or duct network.
Avoid: luxury spa design, shiny modern glass shower cabins, photographic materials, busy noise, exaggerated roof height, extra rooms, extra showerheads, plants, hospital symbols, huge empty room, tiny character, thick prison wall cap, mismatched architecture between the two views, game HUD, inventory UI, arrows, watermarks, decorative border. Final polished concept, cohesive perspective and proportions.

Preserve the ENTIRE RIGHT closed-roof panel and both headings exactly. Maintain the same crisp hand-painted game artwork. No other changes, no added showers or people, no arrows or callout labels.
